correctness.rationale: An induced named K4-free base has one nonalgebraic one-point type for each allowed adjacency pattern: the new vertex creates a K4 exactly when its proposed neighborhood contains a triangle. The extension property realizes each allowed diagram over that very base, and homogeneous quantifier elimination distinguishes no further types within it. An independent exhaustive census of edge masks rejected four-sets with all four triangles, counted triangle-free subsets, then tested ambient-n normalized coefficients by exact rational arithmetic. The admissible counts for n=0,...,6 were 1,1,2,8,63,958,27626; all 72 failures occur at n=6 and only k=4. The forced degree signature (3,3,3,3,3,5) leaves a 2-regular five-vertex graph after removing the hub, necessarily C5. There are 6*5!/10=72 labelled wheels. Their generating function is (1+z)^5+z(1+5z+5z^2), yielding b3=3/4, b4=1/3, b5=1/6 and reversal gap 1/72. The zero b6 is included with ambient n=6; the test is not degree-normalized.
residual_risks: The census is exhaustive only through six named vertices. It makes no further assertion about larger bases.

originality.rationale: The accepted increment is the complete first-failure classification with ambient binomial normalization. The triangle-free complex, type-to-diagram correspondence, and general notion of ultra-log-concavity are established inputs. value.rationale: Sizes of admissible named neighborhoods give a natural rank sequence; ambient binomial scaling compares the fractions of all neighborhoods of each size that are allowed. The result locates the first obstruction to this strengthened log-concavity, isolates one graph rather than offering an isolated failure, and gives an exact, reproducible witness. The unnormalized wheel sequence does not show the obstruction.
residual_risks: The classification concerns this specific normalization and the first possible size, not a general characterization of log-concavity for higher orders.
